memory_candidates.content: When a fix requires moving a decision earlier in a long orchestration script (a 'hoist'), re-run the FULL test suite after each phase, not just the targeted group -- an accidental ordering shield between two previously-independent guards (e.g. a content-hash streak check that always ran against a freshly-minted value before an older, later-positioned replay check could fire) can silently break once the hoist removes the ordering that kept them from ever colliding. Root-cause with a minimal standalone repro harness (copy only the collaborators actually needed) rather than debugging inside the full fixture suite.

Adding a production check that reads a composed artifact's own content back (rather than only comparing state files) can expose that long-lived test doubles/stubs for that artifact's producer never bothered to write real content, since nothing previously read it back. Before adding such a check, grep the whole suite for every stub definition of the relevant collaborator and upgrade each to produce realistic, byte-compatible content -- otherwise the new check will correctly-but-noisily flag every unrelated fixture as a 'missing/invalid artifact' case.

On NixOS, a deployed shellcheck binary path under /nix/store can go stale (GC'd) even though `shellcheck` was previously on PATH. Fallback: `nix-shell -p shellcheck --run "shellcheck ..."` reliably fetches/launches a working binary without needing to fix the stale profile entry.
